FULL.notes:
[chunk 1/5] KEY SIFI FINDINGS: (1) HIDDEN LEVERAGE — Meta has committed to a 20% stake in a Louisiana data center campus JV with $27B total capex and embedded $28B residual value guarantees (RVGs) on operating leases commencing 2029. Total max exposure is $45.99B (~11.6% of total assets). RVGs decrease over time but create contingent obligation. (2) VIE RISK — Meta is not the primary beneficiary of the Louisiana Venture (lacks power to direct activities most significantly impacting economics), so JV is unconsolidated. Co-owner identity is NOT disclosed. (3) EXECUTION RISK — Leases commence 2029, requiring 4 years of construction completion and tenant negotiations. No contracted revenue backlog disclosed to offset capex and RVG exposure. (4) COST OPACITY — RVG is contingent and "not probable," so no liability recorded. However, at 20-year horizon, fair value of data center assets may be volatile, creating tail risk. (5) CAPEX-ROI GAP — $27B capex commitment to serve "future infrastructure capacity needs as AI markets and technologies develop" but no specific customer contracts or revenue commitments disclosed. Timing and volume uncertain. Meta is not naming the co-sponsor of the Venture, creating counterparty visibility gap. The restricted cash escrow of $5B related to a "multi-year purchase agreement" (Note 4) likely relates to this or another cloud compute obligation but is not explicitly tied to the Louisiana JV in this excerpt."
[chunk 2/5] Meta 10-Q Q1 2026: Extracted capex commitments (~$459B total non-cancelable spend through 2036), off-balance-sheet data-center co-development vehicle, and regulatory/litigation risks including $62.85B penalty exposure (New Mexico), DMA fines ($200M EUR), and abuse-of-dominance judgments ($542M EUR). Two key SIFI signals: (1) CAPEX_ROI_GAP—massive infrastructure spend ($237.67B contractual + $182.88B leases) with no disclosed revenue-matching contracts from hyperscaler customers; (2) COST_OPACITY—servers/network depreciation doubled YoY without explanation of asset life or valuation assumptions. Private counterparties to cloud/infrastructure deals are unnamed, limiting supply-chain transparency. Youth litigation exposure (bellwether trials ongoing, potential multi-billion abatement costs) and European regulatory uncertainty (DSA compliance questions on minor protection) pose material downside to European revenue and user experience.
[chunk 3/5] SIFI-Material Extraction from META 10-Q (Q1 2026). Key findings: (1) CAPEX_ROI_GAP: Meta has significantly increased infrastructure capex (Q1 2026: $19.84B) and unrecognized RSU/option expense ($79.22B expected to vest over 3 years), with large committed spend on AI initiatives, cloud capacity, and Reality Labs ($4.03B Q1 loss expected to persist), but no quantified contracted revenue uplift disclosed. (2) REVENUE_ROUNDTRIP: Reels monetizes at structurally lower rate than Feed/Stories—investments in Reels growth/promotion do not generate equivalent ad revenue. (3) SUPPLIER_CONCENTRATION: Critical dependency on Apple iOS (largest platform) and Google (browser/Android) for ad delivery—both have restricted data signaling used in targeting, adversely impacting advertiser budgets. (4) COST_OPACITY: $17.82B unrecognized tax benefits / $15.89B IRS 2017-2019 transfer pricing claim creates material contingent liability and earnings volatility. (5) Tax Court ruled Meta's IP transfer undervalued by $1.48B (2010 tax year), signaling systematic underestimation of IP transfer pricing. (6) Regulatory headwinds (EU DSA, GDPR, privacy laws, Apple/Google platform changes) are quantifiably eroding ad targeting capability. (7) Reality Labs represents long-term capex bet on products "only realized next decade"—classic execution risk / ROI gap. NOTE: No off-balance-sheet SPVs, no circular investments, no counterparty round-tripping detected in this filing section.
